cards.text: Before David is king over Israel, he's on the run, banished from the presence of Saul, Israel's king. But some mighty men come to David, men who help him in battle. I know banished, friend: years in the back of a junk drawer, and NOBODY who landed back there with me came by choice.

cards.question: David is still banished from Saul. Where does this first group of helpers come to him?

cards.text: Ziklag. And these aren't just any helpers. They're archers who sling stones and shoot arrows.

cards.question: What makes these archers who came to David stand out?

answers.text: They use both right and left hands
They shoot from the backs of horses
They can hit targets in the dark

cards.question: True or false: these archers who came to David are Saul's own kinsmen from the tribe of Benjamin.

cards.text: SAUL'S OWN RELATIVES! That's like the guy trying to get you fired, and his own cousin walks up to your desk asking where to sign.
Then the text names 23 of these men, starting with Ahiezer their chief. One standout is Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the Thirty and a leader over the Thirty.

Next, some Gadites, men from the tribe of Gad, defect to David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They're trained for battle, with faces like the faces of lions, and they're as swift as gazelles on the mountains.

cards.question: These Gadites who defect to David are experts with two weapons: the shield and the ___.

cards.text: Then come their eleven leaders, ranked in order, from Ezer the chief down to Machbanai the eleventh. Two of them are named Jeremiah, the fifth AND the tenth, so somebody yells "JEREMIAH!" and half the leadership turns around.

cards.question: These eleven Gadites were army commanders. How strong was the least of them?

answers.text: A match for a hundred men

cards.question: These Gadites also crossed the Jordan River in the first month. True or false: the river was low and calm when they crossed.

cards.text: The Jordan was overflowing ALL its banks, and they crossed it anyway, while I panic when my dough rises a little too fast. Then they put to flight everyone in the valleys, east and west.
Then more Benjamites and some men from Judah come to David's stronghold, and David goes out to meet them.

cards.question: David meets this new group of Benjamites and men from Judah outside his stronghold. What does he want to know?

answers.text: Whether they came in peace or to betray him
Whether they had fought the Philistines before
Whether they could use a sling and a bow

cards.question: True or false: David tells this group that if they came to betray him, he'll strike them down himself.

cards.text: David leaves that to God: if they betray him, may the God of their fathers see it and judge them. Then the Spirit comes upon Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he answers.

cards.question: The Spirit comes upon Amasai, and he speaks for the group. What does he tell David?

answers.text: We are yours and we are with you
We will wait and see what Saul does
We came to ask you for land

cards.question: Amasai wishes peace to David and peace to his helpers. Why? He says it's because David's ___ helps him.
Amasai pledges his group to David. True or false: David receives them and makes them leaders of his troops.

cards.text: Next, some men from Manasseh defect to David when David goes with the Philistines, a people at war with Saul, to fight against Saul. But the Philistine rulers talk it over and send David away.

cards.question: The Philistine rulers send David away instead of letting him fight Saul with them. Why?

answers.text: They fear he'll switch back to Saul
They think his men are too few
They want him to guard their cities

cards.text: They tell each other, "It will cost us our heads if he defects to his master Saul." That's the team that benches you because they're scared you'll score for the other side.

So the men of Manasseh never help the Philistines, and when David goes to Ziklag, seven chiefs of thousands defect to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu and Zillethai. TWO named Jozabad, friend, and I thought the two Jeremiahs were bad.

cards.question: These Manasseh chiefs are mighty men of valor and army commanders. Who do they help David fight?

cards.text: And it doesn't stop there. Men keep coming to help David, day after day.

cards.question: Men keep coming to David day after day until he has a great army. What army does the text say it's like?

cards.text: Then the text counts the men armed for battle who come to David at Hebron. My planet's only big enough for one bakery, and this crowd would need a second planet just to park.

cards.question: Why do all these armed men come to David at Hebron?

answers.text: To turn Saul's kingdom over to him
To win back the town of Ziklag

cards.question: True or false: these men come to turn the kingdom over to David in accordance with the word of the LORD.

cards.text: Then come the numbers, tribe by tribe, from Judah's 6,800 with shields and spears all the way to 120,000 from east of the Jordan. One standout: from Issachar come men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do.
All these men of war come to Hebron arrayed for battle, and they all want the same thing.

cards.question: The men of war came to Hebron fully determined to make David ___ over all Israel.
True or false: all the rest of the Israelites were divided about making David king.

cards.text: Then they spend three days at Hebron eating and drinking with David. Not three hours. THREE. DAYS. I can't keep a batch of cookies alive three MINUTES once a baker smells them.

cards.question: Three days of eating and drinking at Hebron takes a lot of supplies. True or false: their relatives had provided for them.

cards.text: Then neighbors come from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali, bringing flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, oxen and sheep on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen. Somebody loaded up a CAMEL, and here I am delivering cookie boxes with my mustache.

cards.question: All those people and all those supplies at Hebron. The passage ends by saying there was ___ in Israel.
